cards.prose: The disciples who ask *Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?* are the same ones who stand in the way when children are brought to him, because *the disciples rebuked them* (Matthew 19:13). Yahusha (Jesus) answers the question a second time, and again he points to the little ones and says the kingdom belongs to such.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) tells the disciples to let the children come, for the kingdom is of such, the same answer he gave when they asked who is greatest.

cards.prose: The disciples are busy with greatness, and the psalmist says the opposite: *neither do I exercise myself in great matters*. He has quieted himself *as a child that is weaned of his mother* (Psalm 131:2), and the psalm ends by turning Yashar'el (Israel) toward hope in Yahuah (the LORD).
cards.member_sentence: The psalmist keeps clear of great matters and quiets himself like a weaned child, the opposite of the disciples' question about who is greatest.

cards.prose: His answer to the disciples begins with turning, *Except ye be converted, and become as little children* (Matthew 18:3). Ephraim, the scattered northern house, asks for the same thing, *turn thou me, and I shall be turned*, and Yahuah (the LORD) answers by calling him a child, *Is Ephraim my dear son? is he a pleasant child?* (Jeremiah 31:20).
cards.member_phrase: Thou hast chastised me, and I was chastised, as a bullock unaccustomed to the yoke: turn thou me, and I shall be turned
cards.member_sentence: Ephraim asks Yahuah (the LORD) to turn him and is then called a pleasant child, which is the turning Yahusha (Jesus) asks of the disciples.

cards.prose: The proverb answers the question the disciples asked. *Riches, and honour, and life* come by humility joined to the fear of Yahuah (the LORD), and the child set in the midst of them is that humility standing in the room.
cards.member_sentence: Honour and life come by humility and the fear of Yahuah (the LORD), the proverb's answer to who is greatest.

cards.prose: The greatest, he says, is the one who humbles himself like the child. Isaiah shows where such a person sits, since the high and lofty One who inhabits eternity says he dwells in the high and holy place *with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit*. The humble are his near neighbours.
cards.member_phrase: I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble
cards.member_sentence: The One who inhabits eternity says he dwells with the contrite and humble, which is where the humbled child stands.

cards.prose: Peter was among the disciples who first heard this answer, and years later he writes it to the elders and the younger, *be clothed with humility*. His reason is the child's greatness turned the other way round, that Elohim (God) *resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble*.
cards.member_phrase: be clothed with humility: for Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble
cards.member_sentence: Peter later tells them to be clothed with humility because Elohim (God) resists the proud, the same teaching put into a letter.

cards.prose: Both sayings use the same word, *offend*, a stone laid in the road to trip a walker. In the Sermon the stone is your own eye, set right beside *Thou shalt not commit adultery* (Matthew 5:27), the commandment of Moses he is guarding. Here the stone is laid before a little one, and the cost is the sea.
cards.member_phrase: it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell
cards.member_sentence: The Sermon uses the same word offend for the eye and the right hand, with the same end in hell for the whole body.

cards.prose: Mark carries the same millstone, but he sets it right after the cup of water given in Yahusha's (Jesus's) name, of which he says *he shall not lose his reward* (Mark 9:41). What is done to the little ones is counted either way, the kindness and the stone laid in their road.
cards.member_phrase: it is better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he were cast into the sea
cards.member_sentence: Mark sets the millstone right after the cup of water given in his name, so what is done to the little ones is counted either way.

cards.prose: Luke gives the woe first, *It is impossible but that offences will come*, and puts the millstone in the next verse. Right behind it comes the other half of Matthew's chapter, *If thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him* (Luke 17:3).
cards.member_sentence: Luke gives the woe on offences and the millstone, then follows straight with rebuking and forgiving a brother.

cards.prose: The fire Yahusha (Jesus) names is the fire Isaiah saw at the end of his book, and Isaiah says what lies in it, *the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me*. The same chapter has all flesh coming to worship *from one sabbath to another* (Isaiah 66:23), so the fire sits at the edge of a kingdom that keeps his days.
cards.member_phrase: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah's closing verse puts the worm and the fire on the carcases of the men who transgressed, the fire the warning in Matthew points to.
cards.flag: Placed in the stumbling-block thread (the valley and its fire) rather than the resurrection thread, since it speaks of the fire, not of the form of the body.

cards.prose: The valley Yahusha (Jesus) names is a real one, the valley of the son of Hinnom, where the children of Yahudah (Judah) built *the high places of Tophet* and burned their sons and daughters, which Yahuah (the LORD) says *I commanded them not*. He renames it in the next verse, *but the valley of slaughter: for they shall bury in Tophet, till there be no place* (Jeremiah 7:32). That valley is the name behind *hell fire* (Matthew 18:9).
cards.member_phrase: And they have built the high places of Tophet, which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire
cards.member_sentence: The valley of the son of Hinnom, where Tophet was built and then renamed the valley of slaughter, is the place Yahusha (Jesus) calls by name.
cards.flag: Placed in the stumbling-block thread with the Gehenna members rather than the resurrection thread.

cards.prose: The Sermon and this chapter weigh it the same way, one member against the whole body. In the Sermon *one of thy members should perish* so that the whole body is not cast into hell, and here the hand or foot is cut off so that a man enters life *halt or maimed*. Either way he goes in with the body he has, short of a member.
cards.member_phrase: it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell
cards.member_sentence: The Sermon weighs one member against the whole body in the same way, so a man enters life short of a member rather than lose all.

cards.prose: Mark says it with the hand alone, *enter into life maimed*, and then spells out the other end, the fire *that never shall be quenched*. The next verse repeats the line, *Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched* (Mark 9:44), so life is entered in the body one has, short of a hand, and the fire is where the whole body goes otherwise.
cards.member_phrase: it is better for thee to enter into life maimed, than having two hands to go into hell
cards.member_sentence: Mark says enter into life maimed and names the fire that is not quenched, the other end of the same saying.

cards.prose: The one who says it is better to enter life maimed shows Thomas his own hands after the rising. *Behold my hands*, he says, and *thrust it into my side*, so the wounds are kept, and the body that comes up is the body that went down.
cards.member_phrase: Reach hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into my side
cards.member_sentence: The risen Yahusha (Jesus) shows Thomas his hands and side, so the wounds are kept and the body rises in the form it had.

cards.prose: A body short of something is not shut out of the house. Yahuah (the LORD) speaks to *the eunuchs that keep my sabbaths* (Isaiah 56:4) and gives them in his house *a name better than of sons and of daughters*. The man cut off from offspring is kept and named, and so the one who enters life maimed is not turned away for the form he carries.
cards.member_phrase: a place and a name better than of sons and of daughters: I will give them an everlasting name, that shall not be cut off
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) gives the eunuch a place and an everlasting name in his house, so a body lacking something is kept and not shut out.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says the angels of the little ones are always before the Father's face. The psalm says what such angels are for, *charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways*, said of the man who has made Yahuah (the LORD) his refuge. So the little one he warns against despising is under a guard.
cards.member_sentence: Angels are given charge over the one who makes Yahuah (the LORD) his refuge, which is what the angels of the little ones do.

cards.prose: Angels in Daniel have names and ranks and take sides. The messenger is held up by *the prince of the kingdom of Persia*, and *Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me*. When Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of angels standing before the Father for the little ones, it is the same kind of host Daniel saw at work for his people.
cards.member_phrase: lo, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me; and I remained there with the kings of Persia
cards.member_sentence: Michael comes to help the messenger against the prince of Persia, so angels stand and contend on behalf of peoples.

cards.prose: Daniel is told that Michael is *your prince*, an angel who stands for his people and holds with the messenger in what is written in the scripture of truth. That is the kind of thing Yahusha (Jesus) says of a little one, that his angels are in heaven before the Father.
cards.member_sentence: Michael is named as the prince of Daniel's people, an angel who stands for them, as angels stand for the little ones.

cards.prose: Hebrews gives the work of such angels in a line. They are *ministering spirits*, sent out to serve those who inherit, and the verse before says none of them was ever told *Sit on my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool* (Hebrews 1:13). The angels who see the Father's face in Matthew are the ones sent out from it.
cards.member_sentence: Hebrews says what angels do, that they are ministering spirits sent forth to serve those who inherit.

cards.prose: The man who leaves the ninety and nine for the strayed one is Yahuah (the LORD) in Ezekiel, who says of the shepherds that failed *Behold, I am against the shepherds* (Ezekiel 34:10) and then takes the search on himself, *will both search my sheep, and seek them out*. His sheep are the ones *that are scattered* (Ezekiel 34:12).
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) says he himself will search for his sheep and seek them out, the Shepherd behind the man who leaves the ninety and nine.

cards.prose: The sheep that has gone astray in the psalm is still holding the commandments, for his last word is *I do not forget thy commandments*. His prayer is *seek thy servant*, and that is the errand of the shepherd in Matthew. The one he goes after has strayed and has not been forgotten.
cards.member_sentence: A lost sheep who has not forgotten the commandments asks to be sought, which is the sheep the shepherd goes after.

cards.prose: The sheep that have gone astray here are *all we*, and the same chapter says whose they are, *for the transgression of my people was he stricken* (Isaiah 53:8). The Shepherd who goes after the strayed one in Matthew is the one who carries what put them out on the mountain, since Yahuah (the LORD) *hath laid on him the iniquity of us all*.
cards.member_phrase: we have turned every one to his own way; and Yahuah (LORD) hath laid on him the iniquity of us all
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) lays the iniquity of the straying sheep on the Shepherd who goes after them.

cards.prose: The lost sheep here are *my people*, and the verses around them say who, *the children of Yashar'el (Israel) shall come, they and the children of Yahudah (Judah) together* (Jeremiah 50:4). Their own shepherds *have caused them to go astray*, so the one that wandered in Matthew's parable is a sheep of that flock, turned away on the mountains by those who should have kept it.
cards.member_sentence: The lost sheep are the people whose own shepherds caused them to go astray, Yashar'el (Israel) and Yahudah (Judah) together.

cards.prose: Luke tells the same story to other hearers. There it answers the Pharisees and scribes who murmured, *This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them* (Luke 15:2), and in Matthew it is told to the disciples about the little ones. Either way the shepherd's answer is the same, that he goes after the one.
cards.member_sentence: Luke tells the same parable of the lost sheep to the Pharisees who murmured that he receives sinners.

cards.prose: Matthew closes the parable with the Father's will, *it is not the will of your Father which is in heaven, that one of these little ones should perish* (Matthew 18:14). Peter says the same will in his own words, that Yahuah (the LORD) is *longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish*. What some count as slowness is the shepherd still out on the mountain.
cards.member_sentence: Peter says Yahuah (the LORD) is not willing that any should perish, the Father's will in the parable put another way.
cards.flag: The verse says 'any' and 'all', but it also says 'us-ward'; I kept to the words of the verse and did not widen it to everyone.

cards.prose: When he sent out the twelve he named whom the sheep are, *the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel)*. The sheep that has gone astray in this parable is one of them, a member of that house, and the shepherd going after it is on the same errand he gave the twelve.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) sends the twelve to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), the flock the strayed sheep belongs to.

cards.prose: He says it in his own mouth, *not sent but unto the lost sheep*, and it is the shepherd of this parable speaking. The woman who hears those words had come crying *thou Son of David* (Matthew 15:22), the title of that house's king, and she answers by worshipping and asking again, *Adonai (Lord), help me* (Matthew 15:25).
cards.member_sentence: He says again that he is sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), the sheep of the parable.
cards.flag: Matthew 15:28 (his answer to her) is not in my packet, so I left her at her own words and did not say more about her.

cards.prose: The first step is already Moses'. *Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart* is set right beside *rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him*, so the word spoken to him alone is how a brother is not hated in silence and his sin is not left sitting on him. It is the commandment kept, with gaining the brother as its aim.
cards.member_sentence: Moses already says to rebuke a neighbour and not hate a brother in the heart, which is the private first step Matthew gives.

cards.prose: When the private word fails, he reaches for the rule Moses gave. *In the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established* (Matthew 18:16) is Deuteronomy's own rule, that one witness cannot rise against a man, and a matter is settled only *at the mouth of two witnesses*.
cards.member_phrase: at the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall the matter be established
cards.member_sentence: A matter is established only at the mouth of two or three witnesses, the rule Yahusha (Jesus) takes up at the second step.
cards.flag: Source verse is 18:15 but the rule is stated at 18:16; I quoted 18:16 in the prose.

cards.prose: Here the matter is already public, *reported commonly*, and Paul writes to the assembly itself, which is the third step of Matthew's order. His complaint is that they had not *rather mourned, that he that hath done this deed might be taken away from among you* (1 Corinthians 5:2).
cards.member_sentence: Paul brings a matter already public before the assembly and wants the man taken away from among them.

cards.prose: The aim of every step is that *thou hast gained thy brother*, and Paul says how it is done by those who are spiritual, *restore such an one in the spirit of meekness*, *considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted*. The word to a brother who has fallen is for bringing him back.
cards.member_sentence: Paul says to restore a fallen brother in meekness, which is the aim of every step, to gain the brother.

cards.prose: Paul gives Timothy the same rule for an elder, no accusation *but before two or three witnesses*. It is the rule of Moses that Yahusha (Jesus) repeated at the second step, and it holds even for a man whose place would make him easy to accuse.
cards.member_sentence: The rule of two or three witnesses is applied to an accusation against an elder.

cards.prose: Here he gives the keys to Peter, and in this chapter the same words go to all the disciples together, with a brother's case and two or three witnesses just before them. So the binding and loosing is a trust held by many and used on a matter that has been established, and not the power of one man over heaven.
cards.member_phrase: whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven
cards.member_sentence: The same words of binding and loosing given to Peter go here to the disciples together.
cards.flag: The old note called this the first statement of binding and loosing to Peter; I kept that and read it with the witnesses of 18:16.

cards.prose: After the rising he sends them as he was sent, *as my Father hath sent me, even so send I you*, and in the verse after he says *Whose soever sins ye remit, they are remitted unto them* (John 20:23). It is the same binding and loosing, carried by those he sends and given by the Father's own sending.
cards.member_phrase: as my Father hath sent me, even so send I you
cards.member_sentence: He sends the disciples as the Father sent him and speaks of sins remitted and retained, the same binding and loosing.

cards.prose: When men from Judæa taught *Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses*, the brethren did not settle it on one voice. There was *no small dissension and disputation* (Acts 15:2), and the matter went up to the apostles and elders at Jerusalem, many mouths and not one, which is the way a hard matter is to be weighed.
cards.member_sentence: When teachers from Judæa said circumcision was needed to be saved, the matter went up to the apostles and elders and not to one man.
cards.flag: Only Acts 15:1-4 is in my packet, so I did not say how the council ruled.

cards.prose: The two who agree are people like these in Malachi, who feared Yahuah (the LORD) and *spake often one to another*. He *hearkened, and heard it*, and a book of remembrance was written, and the same chapter ends with him telling the righteous from the wicked, *between him that serveth Elohim (God) and him that serveth him not* (Malachi 3:18).
cards.member_phrase: Then they that feared Yahuah (LORD) spake often one to another: and Yahuah (LORD) hearkened, and heard it
cards.member_sentence: Those who feared Yahuah (the LORD) and spoke to one another were heard by him and written in a book of remembrance.
cards.flag: Old note quoted the verse only; I read the agreement of 18:19 as the agreement of the fearing, tied to the witnesses.

cards.prose: The one who says there *am I in the midst of them* (Matthew 18:20) says at the end *lo, I am with you alway*. The presence is tied to a task, *Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you*, so the two or three who stand in his name are the ones keeping what he commanded.
cards.member_sentence: He promises to be with them to the end, while they teach to observe all that he commanded.

cards.prose: The man he made whole is told *sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee*. What the Father does at the Son's hand comes with the commandment, *My Father worketh hitherto, and I work* (John 5:17), so what two agree to ask is not a blank cheque for anything at all.
cards.member_sentence: The man made whole is told to sin no more, so what the Father does at the Son's hand comes with the commandment.
cards.flag: The old note quotes 1 John 5:14 (*if we ask any thing according to his will*) but the card points to John 5:14; I wrote to John 5:14 and its context.

cards.prose: The two or three of the next verse have him *there am I in the midst of them* (Matthew 18:20), and Hebrews gives that presence its promise, *I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee*. The writer rests it on the one who does not change, *Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever* (Hebrews 13:8).
cards.member_phrase: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee
cards.member_sentence: The promise never to leave or forsake is the presence of the one who is the same yesterday, today and for ever.

cards.prose: Lamech boasts that Cain's sevenfold vengeance is small beside his own, *truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold* (Genesis 4:24). Peter offers seven times, and Yahusha (Jesus) answers *Until seventy times seven* (Matthew 18:22), taking the number out of Lamech's mouth and spending it on forgiveness.
cards.member_phrase: I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt
cards.member_sentence: Lamech's seventy and sevenfold vengeance is the number Yahusha (Jesus) turns into forgiveness.

cards.prose: Luke has the same count, and he keeps the order Moses set, *rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him*. The next verse puts Peter's seven into the brother's mouth, *seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to thee, saying, I repent* (Luke 17:4), and the answer is still to forgive.
cards.member_sentence: Luke has the same count with rebuke first and forgiveness when the brother repents.

cards.prose: Peter asks how often a brother may be forgiven, and the psalm gives the pattern behind the answer, Yahuah (the LORD) who is *slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy*. Two verses on it says *He hath not dealt with us after our sins* (Psalm 103:10), which is the king's pardon before the servant went out and took his fellow by the throat.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) is merciful, slow to anger and plenteous in mercy, the pattern behind the king's pardon.

cards.prose: Micah asks who is like Yahuah (the LORD), *that pardoneth iniquity*, and the pardon is for *the remnant of his heritage*, his own people. The brother Peter is asked to forgive is one of them, and the king in the parable does as Micah says, passing by the debt because he *delighteth in mercy*.
cards.member_phrase: Who is a Elohim (God) like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity, and passeth by the transgression of the remnant of his heritage
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) pardons iniquity for the remnant of his heritage and delights in mercy, as the king does in the parable.

cards.prose: He gave the lesson in one line in the Sermon, *your heavenly Father will also forgive you* when men forgive each other, and the next verse says the reverse. The king and his two servants are that line told as a story, and it ends the same way, *So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you* (Matthew 18:35).
cards.member_sentence: The Sermon puts the king's lesson in a line, that the Father forgives those who forgive.

cards.prose: The Sermon's warning, *Judge not, that ye be not judged*, is told here as a story. The servant who would not forgive a hundred pence meets the rule in *with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you again* (Matthew 7:2), and the debt he was forgiven comes back on him.
cards.member_sentence: The warning not to judge comes back on the servant, who is measured by his own measure.

cards.prose: James puts the parable in one sentence, *judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy*, and he sets it under law, since the verse before speaks of being judged *by the law of liberty* (James 2:12). The servant gets that judgment, and the verse ends on the other side of it, *mercy rejoiceth against judgment*.
cards.member_sentence: James says judgment without mercy falls on the one who showed none, while mercy rejoices against judgment.

cards.prose: Paul's *even as* is the lord's question in the parable, *even as I had pity on thee* (Matthew 18:33). Be *tenderhearted*, he says, forgiving one another because Elohim (God) has forgiven, which is the order of the story, mercy received first and then mercy owed.
cards.member_sentence: Paul tells them to forgive as Elohim (God) has forgiven, which is the order of the parable.

cards.prose: Paul has a quarrel in view, as the parable does, and he tells those who have one to bear with each other and forgive, *even as Messiah (Christ) forgave you, so also do ye*. That *so also do ye* is the king's verdict on the servant, who was forgiven much and would not forgive a hundred pence.
cards.member_sentence: Paul tells those with a quarrel to forgive as Messiah (Christ) forgave, which is the servant's duty in the parable.

cards.prose: The servant who would not hear his fellow's plea, *Have patience with me* (Matthew 18:29), is the man in the proverb who *stoppeth his ears*. The proverb says he will cry himself and *shall not be heard*, and the parable shows the same turn, the lord who heard him once now handing him over.
cards.member_sentence: The one who stops his ears at a cry will cry himself and not be heard, as the unforgiving servant finds.

cards.prose: In the parable each servant falls down and asks, and one is heard and the other refused. James tells brothers to *Confess your faults one to another* and *pray one for another, that ye may be healed*, and the verse before says *if he have committed sins, they shall be forgiven him* (James 5:15).
cards.member_sentence: James has brothers confess to each other and pray, and says sins committed are forgiven.

new_threads.title: Binding and loosing on the word of two or three witnesses
new_threads.summary_md:
It ain't new. The binding and loosing in this chapter is the court of Moses, and Yahusha (Jesus) is speaking from inside it. He has just said what is done when a brother will not hear the private word:

*But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.* (Matthew 18:16)

That is Deuteronomy's own rule, and it was old when he said it:

*One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity, or for any sin, in any sin that he sinneth: at the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall the matter be established.* (Deuteronomy 19:15)

In Moses the matter then goes before a court, where the two sides stand in the presence of Yahuah (the LORD) himself:

*Then both the men, between whom the controversy is, shall stand before Yahuah (LORD), before the priests and the judges, which shall be in those days;* (Deuteronomy 19:17)

Then Yahusha (Jesus) hands the verdict to the disciples together, in words he had spoken to Peter alone:

*Verily I say unto you, Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever ye shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.* (Matthew 18:18)

So the binding and loosing is the judgment of a matter that has been heard on its witnesses, and it is carried by the ones he sends, as he says after the rising:

*Whose soever sins ye remit, they are remitted unto them; and whose soever sins ye retain, they are retained.* (John 20:23)

Then comes the verse that is so often lifted out of its place:

*For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.* (Matthew 18:20)

Read where he put it, these are the two or three witnesses of verse sixteen, standing where Moses stood the two men, before Yahuah (the LORD) and the judges, and he is in the midst of that hearing. Malachi shows the kind of people who are heard when they speak to one another:

*Then they that feared Yahuah (LORD) spake often one to another: and Yahuah (LORD) hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared Yahuah (LORD), and that thought upon his name.* (Malachi 3:16)

Nothing here turns a gathering into a room where anything asked is granted, and nothing gives men a power over heaven. A matter established on the mouth of witnesses is bound as the Torah already binds it, and the one who sits in the midst of it is the one who gave the rule.
